accepted_examples.german: Es gibt keinen Weg hier heraus. Wir sitzen in der Falle.
accepted_examples.english: There's no way out of here. We're trapped.
accepted_examples.note: heraus means out from a place; the phrase here heraus gives a clear local direction.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist mir unmöglich, dir zu helfen.
accepted_examples.english: It is impossible for me to help you.
accepted_examples.note: unmöglich is an adjective meaning impossible; the example uses it predicatively after ist.

accepted_examples.german: Sie ist der Liebling des Lehrers.
accepted_examples.english: She's the teacher's pet.
accepted_examples.note: Liebling means a person especially favored by someone; Duden gives der Liebling des Lehrers as an example.

accepted_examples.german: Ist es tatsächlich das, was Tom gesagt hat?
accepted_examples.english: Is that really what Tom said?
accepted_examples.note: tatsächlich means actually or really in this question.

accepted_examples.german: Er kam, um uns um Hilfe zu bitten.
accepted_examples.english: He came to ask us for our help.
accepted_examples.note: bitten um Hilfe means to ask for help.

accepted_examples.german: Ich werde den Wagen und den Hund behalten.
accepted_examples.english: I'll keep the car and the dog.
accepted_examples.note: behalten means to keep items in one's possession.

accepted_examples.german: Der Supermarkt bei uns in der Nähe hat letzte Woche dichtgemacht.
accepted_examples.english: The supermarket near our house closed last week.
accepted_examples.note: in der Nähe means nearby or in the vicinity.

accepted_examples.german: Wann hast du jemals etwas für mich getan?
accepted_examples.english: When have you ever done anything for me?
accepted_examples.note: jemals means ever; the selected sentence is correctly punctuated.

accepted_examples.german: Mach das nicht! Es ist dumm und gefährlich.
accepted_examples.english: Don't do it! It's stupid and dangerous.
accepted_examples.note: gefährlich is a predicative adjective describing the action.

accepted_examples.german: Wie weit ist es von hier zum Hotel?
accepted_examples.english: How far is it from here to the hotel?
accepted_examples.note: Hotel is used as a straightforward destination noun.

accepted_examples.german: Tom ist ein Meister der Verkleidung.
accepted_examples.english: Tom is a master of disguise.
accepted_examples.note: Meister means someone highly skilled in a field.

accepted_examples.german: Wie bist du in den Kampf verwickelt worden?
accepted_examples.english: How did you get involved in the fight?
accepted_examples.note: Kampf refers to a fight or struggle in this question.

accepted_examples.german: Das Mädchen ist geschickt im Stricken.
accepted_examples.english: The girl is skillful at knitting.
accepted_examples.note: geschickt is an adjective meaning skillful; here it follows ist.

accepted_examples.german: Das Mehl sieben, um die Klumpen zu entfernen.
accepted_examples.english: Sift the flour to remove the lumps.
accepted_examples.note: sieben means to sift or sieve; the imperative-style instruction is natural in a recipe.

accepted_examples.german: Tom kann nicht gewinnen, und er weiß das.
accepted_examples.english: Tom can't win and he knows it.
accepted_examples.note: gewinnen means to win or be victorious.

accepted_examples.german: Es kommt mir dumm vor, das zu tun.
accepted_examples.english: It seems stupid to me to do that.
accepted_examples.note: dumm is used predicatively to describe the action.

accepted_examples.german: Sie war erschrocken beim Anblick der Leiche.
accepted_examples.english: She was scared at the sight of the dead body.
accepted_examples.note: Leiche means a dead body; the example directly illustrates the noun.

accepted_examples.german: Ich bin ein Agent.
accepted_examples.english: I'm an agent.
accepted_examples.note: Agent is used as a simple noun for a person acting on behalf of an organization or client.

accepted_examples.german: Toms Traum ist ein Leben in den Bergen.
accepted_examples.english: Tom's dream is to live in the mountains.
accepted_examples.note: Traum means a dream or aspiration in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist sogar noch schlimmer, als ich dachte.
accepted_examples.english: It's even worse than I thought.
accepted_examples.note: schlimmer is the comparative form meaning worse.

accepted_examples.german: Während du fort warst, ist eine Menge passiert.
accepted_examples.english: A lot's happened while you've been away.
accepted_examples.note: fort means away in this temporal clause.

accepted_examples.german: Wir waren in Gefahr, ums Leben zu kommen.
accepted_examples.english: We were in danger of losing our lives.
accepted_examples.note: Gefahr means danger and appears in the common phrase in Gefahr sein.

accepted_examples.german: Wir hatten damit absolut nichts zu tun.
accepted_examples.english: We had absolutely nothing to do with that.
accepted_examples.note: absolut intensifies the negative phrase and means absolutely.

held_examples.german: Es scheint nur einen einzigen Weg hier heraus zu geben.
held_examples.reason: Valid near-duplicate of the selected phrase; the chosen example adds a complete, clear context.

held_examples.german: Das ist tatsächlich eine wirklich gute Idee.
held_examples.reason: Valid but redundantly uses tatsächlich and wirklich together; the selected question is more concise.

held_examples.german: Tom kam, um uns um Hilfe zu bitten.
held_examples.reason: Valid near-duplicate of the selected example; keep one primary pair.

held_examples.german: Wir wollen es erst einmal für uns behalten.
held_examples.reason: This is the figurative keep-a-secret sense, not the target possession/retention sense.

held_examples.german: Hast du jemals daran gedacht das zu tun?
held_examples.reason: The extended infinitive clause requires a comma after gedacht; use the other correctly punctuated candidate.

held_examples.german: Hast du eine Ahnung, wie gefährlich das ist?
held_examples.reason: Valid but longer; the selected imperative is a direct, self-contained example.

held_examples.german: Bitte hol mich um sechs vom Hotel ab.
held_examples.reason: Valid but longer than the selected concise location question.

held_examples.german: Er hat seinen Meister gefunden.
held_examples.reason: This is an idiom meaning he met his match, not the skillful-master sense taught by the entry.

held_examples.german: Es war ein Kampf wie um Leben und Tod.
held_examples.reason: Valid but the simile adds complexity; the selected sentence shows the noun in a direct question.

held_examples.german: Tom sollte in der Lage sein zu gewinnen.
held_examples.reason: The extended infinitive clause should be set off with a comma before zu gewinnen.

held_examples.german: Wer wäre dumm genug, um das zu tun?
held_examples.reason: Valid, but the selected example demonstrates dumm in a simple opinion construction.

held_examples.german: Tom bekam Angst, als er die Leiche sah.
held_examples.reason: Valid alternate but more graphic and less direct than the selected sentence.

held_examples.german: Nur damit ihr’s wisst: Ich bin Agent des Bundesfahndungsamts!
held_examples.reason: The institution name is not the standard German agency name and is not a clean transferable example.

held_examples.german: Die Zeit kommt, wenn dein Traum wahr wird.
held_examples.reason: Valid but less idiomatic/straightforward than the selected sentence about an aspiration.

held_examples.german: Es sieht viel schlimmer aus, als es ist.
held_examples.reason: Valid alternate; the selected sentence is more self-contained.

held_examples.german: Regen, Regen gehe fort, geh an einen anderen Ort.
held_examples.reason: A nursery-rhyme line; the selected sentence shows the ordinary away sense.

held_examples.german: Er hat es auf eigene Gefahr hin getan.
held_examples.reason: Valid fixed phrase, but less direct than the selected sentence about being in danger.

held_examples.german: Tom war absolut von sich selbst überzeugt.
held_examples.reason: Valid but context-heavy; the selected phrase makes the adverb's scope clearer.

held_examples.german: Die Polizei klagte ihn wegen Mord an.
held_examples.reason: The standard construction is wegen Mordes or wegen des Mordes; this candidate is missing the required form.

held_examples.german: Tom stritt ab, an dem Mord beteiligt gewesen zu sein.
held_examples.reason: Grammatical German, but the supplied translation loses the past-time meaning; replaced with a short, precise example.

editorial_examples.note: Original example using the standard genitive after wegen and a precise English translation.

plural_reviews.note: Sturm meaning a strong wind forms the plural Stürme.
Null meaning the numeral zero forms the plural Nullen.
Both plural forms are attested for the borrowed currency noun: Pennys for individual coins and Pence for a sum/denomination.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Pennys counts individual coins; Pence is used for a sum or denomination in British currency.

plural_reviews.note: Abteilung forms the plural Abteilungen.
Papiere is the plural for sheets, documents, or kinds; bulk paper as a material is ordinarily singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Papiere is used for individual documents/sheets or kinds. Papier as a material is usually singular.

plural_reviews.note: Genie forms the plural Genies.
Pater in the religious-order sense has the Latin plural Patres.
Wolf forms the plural Wölfe.
Both Pizzas and Pizzen are accepted plural forms.
Mittage is the plural for separate noon periods or days; the ordinary time-of-day sense is usually singular.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Mittage for multiple separate days/noon periods; Mittag as the time of day is commonly singular.

plural_reviews.note: Sack meaning a large bag forms Säcke.
Mittel meaning an agent, means, or appliance has an unchanged plural form Mittel.
Both forms occur; Obersten is the more usual plural, while Oberste is less common.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Plural is usually Obersten; Oberste is a less common variant. The noun denotes the military rank colonel.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Gnaden but marks the plural rare.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Rare plural; Gnade is normally singular in the sense of mercy or grace.

plural_reviews.note: Duden gives Viren as the standard German plural. Vira is a New Latin form, while Virus(s)e is not the standard form for this learner entry.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Viren in standard German, regardless of the article der/das in singular. Do not use Latin Vira in ordinary German.

plural_reviews.note: Feld meaning a plot of open land forms Felder.
Duden gives Hämmer for the tool sense; remove Hammer as a distractor form.
Duden lists Kommandos and, in Austria, Kommanden. Kommanda is not a standard German plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Kommandos is standard; Kommanden is an Austrian variant. The sense 'command authority' has no plural.

plural_reviews.note: Krankenwagen has the same form in singular and plural.
For the masculine person/leader sense, the plural is unchanged Leiter; do not confuse with feminine die Leiter (ladder), plural Leitern.
Cent stays unchanged in price/amount expressions; Cents is used when counting individual coins.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Cent after a number in an amount (fünf Cent). Cents can count separate physical coins.

plural_reviews.value: Usually singular in this material sense
plural_reviews.note: Holz as a material is a mass noun and usually singular; Hölzer refers to types or pieces of wood.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Usually singular for wood as a material. Hölzer is possible for types or individual pieces.

plural_reviews.note: Stern meaning a celestial star forms Sterne.
Lippe forms the plural Lippen.
